method: Bounded verse-level preliminary comparison against Quran.com/legacy.quran.com and accessible primary-text translations. Original Hebrew and Greek critical editions, manuscript witnesses, and publication security not independently checked. Candidates must remain unpublished. This batch does not certify exhaustive source absence.

verses.finding: Final reckoning and fair recompense; no specific earlier passage established in this bounded screening.
Written deferred-debt agreements, scribes, and witnesses; Deuteronomy 19:15 is a general legal-witness comparison, not an equivalent contract procedure.
Travel without a scribe, security pledge, trust, and testimony; Deuteronomy 24:10–13 regulates the handling of a debtor's pledge but does not prescribe this Qur'anic travel procedure.
God owns heavens and earth and accounts for concealed thoughts; no precise earlier passage established in this bounded screening.
Belief in God, angels, books, and messengers and the formula of obedience; no precise earlier textual parallel established in this bounded screening.
Divine obligation within human capacity and prayer for mercy; 1 Corinthians 10:13 addresses bearable temptation rather than the scope of legal/religious obligation.

candidates.shared: Witnesses as part of evidentiary reliability.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy addresses testimony in accusations and requires two or three witnesses; Qur'an 2:282 addresses deferred-debt documentation and includes detailed witness composition and scribal requirements.

candidates.shared: A pledge associated with a loan or obligation.
candidates.difference: Deuteronomy protects a debtor against intrusive seizure and requires returning a poor person's cloak at night; Qur'an 2:283 addresses travel without a scribe, security, trust, and concealing testimony.

candidates.shared: God does not subject believers to an unbearable ordeal.
candidates.difference: Paul addresses temptation and endurance, while Qur'an 2:286 concerns the capacity for imposed responsibility, moral accountability, and a communal prayer.
